tung-lo-mo-an-giang.name: Tung Lò Mò Chăm Beef Sausage, An Giang
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.serving_basis: Serves 4 with rice or vermicelli and fresh vegetables.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.description: Tung lò mò is a beef sausage associated with the Chăm community in An Giang, usually grilled until its casing turns fragrant and lightly browned. Bếp Việt’s home version uses a ready-made product, cooks it through, and serves it with fresh vegetables.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.finished_dish: Golden grilled tung lò mò with a juicy center, served with fresh herbs and cucumber.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.excerpt: Golden grilled tung lò mò with a juicy center, served with fresh herbs and cucumber.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.serving: Cut the sausage diagonally after grilling and serve with fresh herbs, cucumber, and rice vermicelli or hot rice. Offer lime-pepper salt on the side.
tips: Choose tung lò mò from a trusted seller and follow the package storage instructions.
Grill over medium heat and turn often so the casing does not burn before the center is hot.
If the product is raw, cook it completely according to the maker’s directions and keep it separate from raw food.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.tip: Choose tung lò mò from a trusted seller and follow the package storage instructions.
tung-lo-mo-an-giang.image_alt: A plate of golden grilled tung lò mò from An Giang, sliced and served with herbs and cucumber.

ingredients.notes: Steamed rice may be used instead.

preparation_steps.instruction: Check the label to see whether the sausage is raw or precooked; thaw in the refrigerator if needed.
Wash and drain the vegetables and cucumber. Mix the salt, pepper, and lime juice.
Preheat a grill or skillet over medium heat.

cooking_steps.instruction: Grill or pan-sear the sausage, turning evenly, until browned and hot through to the center according to the package directions.
Rest for a few minutes, then slice diagonally into bite-sized pieces.
Serve with fresh vegetables, cucumber, and rice vermicelli or rice; keep the lime-pepper salt on the side.

tung-lo-mo-an-giang.time_note: Heating time varies with the sausage diameter and whether it is raw or precooked; follow the package instructions.

goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.name: An Giang Sầu Đâu Salad with Dried Snakehead
aliases: Sầu Đâu Leaf and Dried Snakehead Salad
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.serving_basis: Serves 4 as a shared salad or light starter.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.description: This An Giang salad pairs the gentle bitterness of sầu đâu leaves with savory dried snakehead, boiled pork, and a sweet-tart tamarind fish-sauce dressing. Bếp Việt mixes it in small batches so the leaves stay fresh and the fish does not break apart.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.finished_dish: Lightly bitter leaves and crisp papaya, savory dried snakehead, and a balanced sweet-sour tamarind dressing.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.excerpt: Lightly bitter leaves and crisp papaya, savory dried snakehead, and a balanced sweet-sour tamarind dressing.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.serving: Toss just before serving and finish with roasted peanuts and herbs. Serve with hot rice or as a starter.
tips: Buy tender sầu đâu leaves from a trusted local source; blanch briefly and taste to manage bitterness.
Grill or pan-cook the dried fish until fragrant, then remove all bones before mixing.
Cool the dressing and add gradually; mix only the amount you plan to serve so the salad does not turn watery.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.tip: Buy tender sầu đâu leaves from a trusted local source; blanch briefly and taste to manage bitterness.
goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.image_alt: An Giang sầu đâu salad with dried snakehead, boiled pork, green papaya, and roasted peanuts.

ingredients.name: Dried snakehead fish
ingredients.notes: Choose moderately salted fish, grill, and remove bones.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Boil through, cool, and slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water and strain.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the dried fish.

preparation_steps.instruction: Wash the sầu đâu leaves, blanch in boiling water for about 10 seconds, rinse in cool water, and drain; taste before using.
Shred the papaya, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze dry. Boil the pork through, cool, and slice thinly.
Grill the dried snakehead over medium heat until fragrant. Cool, remove tough skin and bones, and flake into small pieces.
Soak the tamarind in warm water and strain; combine the juice with fish sauce, sugar, garlic, and chili.

cooking_steps.instruction: Taste the dressing and adjust the sweet-sour balance. Reduce fish sauce if the dried fish is salty.
Place the leaves, papaya, pork, and fish in a wide bowl. Add dressing a little at a time and toss gently.
Add Vietnamese coriander, transfer to a plate, and sprinkle with peanuts. Serve as soon as it is mixed.

goi-sau-dau-kho-ca-loc-an-giang.time_note: Preparation time depends on the saltiness and dryness of the fish; soak it according to the seller’s directions if needed.

be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.name: Cầu Mống Roast Veal, Quảng Nam
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.serving_basis: Serves 4; roll the veal with fresh herbs, rice paper, and anchovy sauce.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.description: Cầu Mống roast veal is known for tender slices with a fragrant golden edge, eaten with fresh herbs, rice paper, and anchovy sauce. Bếp Việt adapts the presentation and rolling style for a smaller oven-roasted cut at home.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.finished_dish: Tender aromatic veal with a golden edge, rolled with herbs and rice paper and dipped in pineapple anchovy sauce.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.excerpt: Tender aromatic veal with a golden edge, rolled with herbs and rice paper and dipped in pineapple anchovy sauce.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.serving: Arrange the veal, herbs, green banana, starfruit, and rice paper in separate groups. Mix pineapple into the anchovy sauce and season with garlic and chili; roll each bite as you eat.
tips: Buy fresh veal from a inspected supplier, keep it chilled, and prevent raw meat from touching ready-to-eat vegetables.
Roast an evenly thick piece; use a food thermometer and let the meat rest before slicing.
Season anchovy sauce gradually because saltiness varies between products.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.tip: Buy fresh veal from an inspected supplier, keep it chilled, and prevent raw meat from touching ready-to-eat vegetables.
be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.image_alt: A platter of Cầu Mống roast veal slices with fresh herbs, rice paper, starfruit, and anchovy sauce.

ingredients.name: Veal
ingredients.notes: Use a uniformly thick loin or leg cut.

ingredients.name: Rice paper
ingredients.notes: Choose thin, pliable sheets for rolling.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Use basil, Vietnamese coriander, and local herbs.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Slice and soak briefly in lightly salted water.

ingredients.name: Anchovy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use ready-to-serve sauce or follow the label directions.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.notes: Brush a thin layer over the meat before roasting.

preparation_steps.instruction: Pat the veal dry, season lightly with salt, and keep chilled while preparing the vegetables. Use a separate board for raw meat.
Wash and drain the herbs; slice the starfruit, green banana, and cucumber. Finely chop the pineapple, garlic, and chili.
Mix the anchovy sauce with pineapple, garlic, chili, and sugar; taste before serving.

cooking_steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Quickly sear all sides of the veal in a hot skillet to develop a golden surface.
Transfer to the oven, reduce to 180°C, and roast until the thickest part reaches at least 63°C; rest for at least 3 minutes.
Slice thinly across the grain. Arrange with the vegetables, herbs, rice paper, and anchovy sauce, and serve immediately.

be-thui-cau-mong-quang-nam.time_note: Roasting time varies with the shape and thickness of the cut; a reliable food thermometer is more accurate than timing alone.

ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.name: Mekong Delta Cá Lóc Nướng Trui
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.serving_basis: Serves 4 as a shared grilled fish, rolled with rice paper and vegetables.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.description: Cá lóc nướng trui is a rustic southern Vietnamese dish, traditionally cooked whole over straw to preserve the fish’s natural sweetness. Bếp Việt adds a home oven method; the fish is cleaned for convenience but its skin is kept intact.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.finished_dish: Fragrant, fully cooked fish with flaky white flesh and lightly charred skin, served with herbs and tamarind fish sauce.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.excerpt: Fragrant, fully cooked fish with flaky white flesh and lightly charred skin, served with herbs and tamarind fish sauce.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.serving: Peel back the charred skin, lift the fish from the bones, and roll it with herbs, cucumber, starfruit, green banana, and rice paper. Serve tamarind fish sauce on the side.
tips: For traditional outdoor roasting, leave the fish whole and scaled and use a safe, well-ventilated fire area.
For home cooking, ask the fish seller to clean the fish while leaving its skin on; roast until the flesh turns opaque and separates easily from the bones.
Keep raw fish and its juices away from ready-to-eat vegetables; use separate boards and tongs.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.tip: For home cooking, ask the fish seller to clean the fish while leaving its skin on; roast until the flesh turns opaque and separates easily from the bones.
ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.image_alt: A whole Mekong Delta cá lóc nướng trui with flaky white flesh, fresh greens, rice paper, and tamarind fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Snakehead fish
ingredients.notes: One medium fish; cleaned for the home-oven method.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Use Vietnamese basil, perilla, Vietnamese coriander, or available herbs.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Slice and soak in lightly salted water.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water and strain.

preparation_steps.instruction: For the home method, ask the fish seller to clean the fish while leaving the skin intact. Rinse briefly and pat very dry; do not marinate.
Wash and drain the herbs; cut the cucumber, starfruit, and green banana. Soak the tamarind in warm water and strain.
Mix the tamarind juice with fish sauce, sugar, garlic, and chili; adjust the sweet-sour balance.

cooking_steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Place the fish on a foil-lined tray and roast for about 25–35 minutes, turning once, depending on size.
Check the thickest part: it should be opaque and separate from the bones; with a food thermometer, the center should reach 63°C.
Rest briefly, open the fish along the back, and lift away the larger bones. Serve hot with rice paper, vegetables, and tamarind fish sauce.

ca-loc-nuong-trui-mien-tay.time_note: Whole fish cooks at different rates depending on size and the oven; check the thickest flesh near the backbone before serving.

cha-ruoi-tu-ky.name: Vietnamese Ragworm Patties (Chả Rươi)
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.serving_basis: Serves 4 as a savory dish with rice or vermicelli and fresh herbs.
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.description: Chả rươi is a seasonal autumn dish from Vietnam’s northern delta, especially associated with Tứ Kỳ in Hải Dương. Ragworms are combined with minced pork, egg, dill, and a little tangerine zest for cakes that are aromatic, tender inside, and golden at the edges. Bếp Việt has edited the quantities for a home skillet, keeping the seasoning light so the ragworm flavor remains distinct.
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.finished_dish: Evenly golden, fully cooked cakes scented with dill and tangerine zest, moist but not crumbly.
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.excerpt: Seasonal ragworm cakes with minced pork, dill, egg, and a bright touch of tangerine zest.
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or vermicelli, fresh herbs, and a gently tart fish-sauce dip. Cut into portions after the cakes have rested for a few minutes.
tips: If using frozen ragworms, thaw them in the refrigerator, remove any debris, and discard any ingredient with an off smell.
Finely grate only a little of the colored tangerine peel to add aroma without bitterness.
Cook moderately thin cakes over medium heat so the center cooks through before the outside becomes too dark.
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.tip: Keep thawed ragworms chilled until mixing, then cook each cake through before serving.
search_terms: Tứ Kỳ Hải Dương ragworm cakes
cha-ruoi-tu-ky.image_alt: A plate of golden Tứ Kỳ ragworm cakes flecked with dill and thin tangerine zest.

ingredients.name: Fresh or frozen ragworms
ingredients.notes: Thaw frozen ragworms safely in the refrigerator.

ingredients.name: Ground pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: A little fat helps keep the cakes tender.

ingredients.name: Tangerine peel
ingredients.notes: Use only the colored zest; slice very thinly.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly so it does not overpower the ragworms.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the saltiness of the fish sauce.

preparation_steps.instruction: If using frozen ragworms, thaw them in the refrigerator. Pick out straw or debris, rinse gently with clean water, and drain; keep chilled while preparing the remaining ingredients.
Wash and drain the dill and scallions, then chop finely. Remove only the colored tangerine zest and slice it very thinly.
Beat the eggs. Gently combine the ragworms with the ground pork, eggs, dill, scallions, tangerine zest, fish sauce, salt, and pepper.

cooking_steps.instruction: Warm a thin layer of oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Spoon the mixture into small cakes and flatten them to about 1 cm thick.
Cook each side for about 3–4 minutes, turning carefully until evenly golden and cooked through. Lower the heat if the outside colors too quickly.
Transfer to paper towels, rest for a few minutes, and serve hot with fresh herbs, rice, or vermicelli.

cha-ruoi-tu-ky.time_note: Cooking time depends on cake thickness and stove heat; cut into one cake to verify the center is fully cooked.
